transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-12-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mike (CTO, Acme), Sara (ML Eng), Jamal (Infra)

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check-in on the POC progress for the Acme pilot, um we have 45 minutes so we'll run through access, the staging benchmark, and any blockers.
00:28 Mike: yep thanks, yeah we had a couple folks pulled in, jamal is on infra, sara on ml, i'm mike. quick note, bit of context, we saw the first benchmark you sent on monday, curious about the quantized run.
00:45 Priya: cool thanks, so the run we did monday was fp16 on a single A100, the quantized int8 profile is still pending because we need staging service account access to the S3 artifacts.
00:58 Jamal: interrupt real quick, we thought we granted access, but turns out the IAM role didn't include s3:GetObject for that bucket, we'll fix that after this call.
01:15 Alex: great, so checklist: iam role, vpc peering, and sample traffic. sara, can you remind us of the token lengths you're seeing in production?
01:34 Sara: yeah, most requests are short, like 8-32 tokens, but we have a tail for recs and summarization up to 512 occasionally. 95th perc is around 280 tokens.
01:50 Priya: that's super helpful, for batching and kv cache planning. if the 95th is 280 we'll keep that in mind, it impacts kernel selection and latency.
02:05 Mike: on the security side, our compliance wants SOC2 evidence and KMS integration. how does Redwood handle KMS/HSM?
02:22 Alex: we have KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for private, also audit logs in the console, i'll share the security pack. note, for hosted pilot we can use Redwoods managed keys but for private you can bring your own.
02:40 Mike: okay good. jamal, you said vpc peering is partially set up?
02:47 Jamal: yes, peering looks ok but the routes weren't propagated to the staging subnet; and we need the specific CIDR for the Redwood egress IPs which we asked for.
03:05 Priya: (murmur) we emailed the egress list last week, i'll re-send; there might be a typo in the csv so i'll double check.
03:20 Alex: let's revisit the initial benchmark numbers, priya can you walk through the key metrics?
03:30 Priya: sure, raw numbers from the fp16 run: avg token latency ~38ms, 95th token latency ~120ms, throughput about 30 reqs/sec with batch size 8 for typical prompts. cost per 1k tokens was estimated at $0.45 on that setup. caveat, those are cold-run numbers and no prefix caching applied.
03:57 Sara: hmm 120ms 95th seems high for short prompts, is that because of batch tail latency?
04:05 Priya: yeah partly; we saw some spike when KV cache misses occurred; with prefix caching the 95th drops to ~70-80ms in our sim.
04:20 Mike: so int8 could reduce cost but what about latency?
04:25 Priya: int8 typically reduces memory and can increase throughput; for some models it actually speeds up token compute by 10-25% but quantization can slightly affect quality. we'll run quality evals with your eval set.
04:45 Sara: yes please, we have 3 eval prompts and a small holdout for quality monitoring. we'll share those.
05:02 Alex: noted. jamal, for the staging infra timeline, can you estimate when IAM and route propagation will be finished?
05:12 Jamal: i can get iam done today, route propagation maybe tomorrow, there's a firewall rule that needs to be updated.
05:24 Mike: ok good. next, any concerns about data residency? some of our data has eu residency requirements.
05:32 Alex: we can route inference to EU region or do private deployment. for POC we can pin region to eu-west if you want.
05:42 Mike: let's keep pilot in US for now, we just want the option later.
05:48 Priya: quick note on the KV cache: if we enable prefix caching for the summarization flow we'll see big token savings for repeated prefixes. recommend we run a second benchmark with caching enabled.
06:05 Sara: yes, our summaries are fairly repetitive so that should help.
06:12 Priya: ok i'll include a caching run.
06:18 Alex: any blockers on providing the sample traffic?
06:22 Sara: i'll anonymize and send it by thursday, it's a small csv with request lengths and spike windows.
06:30 Priya: sweet.
06:34 06:45 Alex: (crosstalk) quick commercial note — pricing for dedicated vs hosted during pilot: hosted usage-based, dedicated has monthly commit; i'll email the worksheet after the call.
06:55 Mike: yes please.
07:05 Priya: back to infra, one more technical item — for the quantized int8 benchmark we need CUDA/cuDNN compatibility on staging, do you run the default AMI or custom?
07:18 Jamal: custom, but it's standard nvidia drivers; i'll confirm the cuda versions, should be fine.
07:28 Priya: if there's a mismatch we can fall back to an fp16 run, but results won't reflect int8 perf.
07:36 Sara: what about memory - any risk of OOM during int8?
07:40 Priya: int8 reduces memory, so it's less likely, but operator kernels depend on model architecture. we'll instrument memory in the run.
07:50 Alex: alright, let's look at timeline items: priya runs quantized + caching benchmark by 2027-01-06, jamal finishes IAM by 2027-01-03, sara sends sample traffic by 2027-01-05, i'll share security pack + pricing by 2027-01-04.
08:10 Mike: sounds good. on compliance deep dive, who should attend from redwood?
08:16 Alex: i'll bring solutions security + product, probably 30 minutes. jamal do you want hte deep dive next week?
08:26 Jamal: yes week of jan 4th works.
08:30 Priya: quick note, we also had a small discrepancy in the first benchmark where one of the tails was due to a model warming call pattern; we recommend running a warmed cache baseline and also a cold-start baseline.
08:45 Sara: good idea. include both, thanks.
09:00 Speaker 1: (inaudible)
09:15 Alex: any open Qs on observability? you can use the console to see token-level breakdowns, i'll share a dashboard link.
09:30 Sara: will the console show per-route cost?
09:35 Alex: yep per-route and per-model, token-type breakdowns and traces.
09:43 Mike: for audit logs we need export to splunk, is that supported?
09:49 Alex: we support syslog and s3 export; for Splunk we can push via syslog or deliver logs to your s3 bucket and you can ingest.
10:05 Priya: while we're on logs, please include a sample request id from your prior logs so we can correlate.
10:12 Sara: i'll pick a few and include them.
10:20 Alex: okay moving on — any blockers with the contract or procurement?
10:26 Mike: procurement is fine for pilot, we may need an addendum for EU data later.
10:33 Alex: noted.
10:40 Priya: small follow-up: for the quantization eval we'll run quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE and also human spot checks) and provide diffs.
10:52 Sara: appreciated.
11:00 Jamal: i have one infra note: our staging is behind a NAT gateway and egress IPs change during scale, how do we handle static allowlists?
11:12 Alex: we can provide a CIDR block for Redwood egress and also support occasional IP rotation; for strict allowlist we recommend VPC peering/private deployment.
11:28 Jamal: ok, i'll document that and capture the firewall rule change.
11:35 Alex: great. do we want to run a quick demo of the console now?
11:40 Mike: not necessary, we'll wait for the benchmark results.
11:46 Priya: final note, i'll attach the exact docker/container image tag we used for the runs and the kernel flags.
11:55 Alex: perfect. any other Qs?
12:02 Mike: none from me.
12:08 Sara: all good.
12:12 Alex: recap of next steps and owners, i'll follow-up in email with the security pack and pricing. thanks everyone.
44:22 End of meeting: total duration ~45 minutes.
